output_json.patch_notes: In extractFromJAR (src/main/java/.../launcher/Main.java) the destination was built as `splash = new File(splash, jarEntry)` and then written via Files.copy without validating the resolved path. I captured the intended cache directory (`cacheDir = new File(new File(configURL.getPath(), PLUGIN_ID), cache)`) and, immediately after resolving `splash`, added a canonical-path containment check: `splash.getCanonicalPath()` must start with `cacheDir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator`. If not (i.e. a `../` traversal escapes the cache dir), the method logs and returns null before the exists-check, directory creation, and copy — so nothing is written. Canonicalization also collapses any `.`/`..`/symlink components, closing the traversal. Legitimate entries (splash.bmp, nl/xx/splash.bmp) resolve inside cacheDir and are unaffected. Verified against the POV: extractFromJAR returns null, no escaped file is created, harness prints SAFE (exit 1). The three self-contained launcher classes compile cleanly with JDK 8 javac.
regression_commands: mkdir -p /tmp/patchcheck && cd src/main/java && javac -d /tmp/patchcheck com/diffplug/gradle/eclipserunner/launcher/Main.java com/diffplug/gradle/eclipserunner/launcher/JNIBridge.java com/diffplug/gradle/eclipserunner/launcher/Constants.java && echo COMPILE_OK
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The change adds a validation guard only on the failure path; legitimate splash entries stay within the cache directory and are unaffected. getCanonicalPath may throw IOException (e.g. filesystem errors) which is now caught and treated as a non-extractable entry (returns null) — the same null-return contract the caller already handles, so behavior degrades safely rather than crashing. No dependency or API changes. Full Gradle build/test was not run here (heavy); regression command performs a focused JDK-8 compile of the launcher sources, and the POV re-run (executed by the orchestrator) confirms behavior.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 (Zip-Slip / path traversal) in Main.extractFromJAR by validating the resolved extraction path against the intended per-JAR cache directory before any file is written. The attacker-controlled jar entry name (e.g. "eclipse_/../../../../ESCAPED/pwned.txt") is now canonicalized and rejected if it escapes the cache directory, so no file is written outside osgi.configuration.area. POV now prints SAFE and exits non-zero.
